Question to ask before buying: What suction mode (max, standard, or quiet) was the published Pa figure measured in?
Why it matters: Published Pa figures are the ceiling, not the daily setting. Hands-on testing we reviewed suggests many robots run well under that ceiling on their default mode, but this isn't a confirmed industry-wide spec, so verify it for your specific model rather than assuming it.

Question to ask before buying: Was the advertised runtime measured at the lowest suction setting?
Why it matters: Runtime drops well below the advertised figure once you switch to a stronger mode for carpet or heavy shedding.

Question to ask before buying: Does it use LiDAR, or camera-only (vSLAM) navigation?
Why it matters: Camera-only navigation struggles more in low light and has a harder time telling objects apart; LiDAR is the current baseline.

Question to ask before buying: Has it been tested specifically around thin-framed furniture (dining chairs, metal-leg stools)?
Why it matters: This is a common blind spot across brands and price points regardless of sensor sophistication.

Question to ask before buying: Is the mop a continuous roller, a spinning disc/pad, or a flat static pad, and how is it rewetted/scraped between passes?
Why it matters: Reported real-world mopping results vary more by maintenance engineering than by mop-type category alone.

Question to ask before buying: Does it auto-empty the dust bin, and how many days between manual bag/filter changes?
Why it matters: Determines real hands-off maintenance frequency, especially for heavy-shedding households.

Question to ask before buying: Does the dock wash and dry mop pads with hot water, or just rinse with cold water?
Why it matters: Hot-water washing and hot-air drying cut down on the odor buildup that plain rinsing doesn't fully solve.

Question to ask before buying: Any published guidance on when battery capacity starts degrading?
Why it matters: Batteries in this category will measurably degrade over time; factor this into a per-year cost comparison.

Question to ask before buying: Are brushes, filters, mop pads, and dust bags sold separately, and at what recurring cost?
Why it matters: Ongoing consumables are a real cost of ownership that doesn't show up in the sticker price.

Question to ask before buying: Who currently owns and services this brand? Any recent bankruptcy, restructuring, or ownership change?
Why it matters: A financially unstable brand is a risk to years of app support, firmware updates, and spare-parts availability.

Question to ask before buying: Does the review or best-of list disclose an affiliate/commission relationship with the products it ranks?
Why it matters: Not disqualifying by itself, but worth weighing against independent, non-commissioned test data when claims conflict.

Question to ask before buying: Is this a vacuum-only, hybrid with mop lift, or hybrid with full mop detach?
Why it matters: Determines whether carpet-specific mop-clearance issues apply to your home at all.
